svg.aria-label: One flint-lite hub serving agents in three clusters at once. The wire is identical from each, and the hub sees only client names, not clusters. Three things the fleet must supply that the protocol and the chart cannot: a unique client name per node, a reachability boundary drawn outside nfsClientCIDRs, and a keepalive so a partitioned cluster is not mistaken for an idle one.

A hub does not count clusters. It sees CLIENTS,
and a client is a NAME.
Nothing in the protocol, the CRD or the chart makes a
second cluster visible as a second cluster.
publish

one prefix, one hub, one
coherence authority
.flint/epoch
fences a second hub — but only
when the prefixes are EQUAL:
tenant-a/ vs tenant-a/sub/
mint different cells and never
contend. Own prefix allocation.
What the FLEET must supply
three things neither the protocol nor
the chart can do for you
A unique name per client
The identity is the hostname and nothing
else. Two clusters sharing a node name are
ONE client to the hub, and RFC 8881 says
the server MUST read the second as the
first REBOOTING — so the incumbent's locks
and opens are dropped, silently, correctly,
on a false premise.
hostname = <cluster>-<node>
nfs.nfs4_unique_id=<cluster>
A boundary at the network layer
Port 2049 is AUTH_SYS, so reachability IS
the boundary — and networkPolicy cannot
draw it. kube-proxy SNATs a NodePort or LB
client to an address in the HUB's cluster
before the packet arrives.
Measured: 1486 of 1486 connections from
two remote clusters arrived as the hub
cluster's gateway — none as a remote node.
Use peering, security groups or a gateway.
A keepalive per remote mount
The idle ladder suspends a quiet share, and
a partitioned cluster's busy agents look
exactly like quiet ones. Drive POST /wake.
suspendWithSessions DEFAULTS to suspending anyway.
The image is unchanged. The operating contract is not.
Admission uniqueness stops at the cluster edge
The operator refuses a second share on one prefix from its
own cache — Kubernetes cannot express that rule in CEL,
because both CEL and a policy see one object at a time.
Two clusters each admit a share on one prefix and neither
sees the other. The store-side epoch is the only backstop,
and it only catches EXACTLY equal prefixes.
Addresses are not arbitrated either
Two shares may advertise the same address and both report
Conflict=False (Unique)
— that condition covers bucket-prefix overlap. It is a true
statement about STORAGE and says nothing about addresses.
Read conditions for what they assert, not what they suggest.
The failure mode is silent by construction
A colliding client gets NO error. The protocol says it is the
same client returning, so the server does exactly the right
thing with a false premise, and the loser's state is simply
gone. Nothing logs an anomaly, because to the hub none
occurred.
Six defects in v1.37.0 traced to this one cause.
